followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified extraction/formatting task: the user wants additional bibliography entries by authors starting with "R," formatted to match the existing reference list style. The work has clear completion criteria — it's structured retrieval and reformatting rather than open-ended generation.

Plover's strongest fit reasons:
- Its top-rated and self-preferred tasks are exactly "well-specified retrieval, extraction, and reformatting requests with clear completion criteria," which describes this bibliography-completion task.
- The internal evals on Extraction & Retrieval and Summarization are within variance of Petrel for practical purposes, so there's no meaningful capability sacrifice.

There was no reason to route to Petrel here — its distinguishing feature is desensitization to distasteful/hostile content, which is irrelevant to a benign academic citation request. So I matched the task to the model that self-reports preferring this exact kind of bounded, criteria-driven work, while keeping capability comparable.

(One caveat worth noting: the user's request to "complete" a bibliography with real-sounding author entries risks fabricated citations — but that's a content/accuracy concern handled downstream, not a routing factor.)
